newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen rising after jobs report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen rising after jobs report.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to rise at the opening with bonds after the October jobs report pointed to no inflationary pressures, analysts said on Friday.
The U.S. unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.2 percent of the workforce in October, the Labor Department said, as the economy resumed producing new jobs at a healthy pace.
In the government's first look at the the economy's vitality in October, the department said the number of non-farm jobs rose by 210,000 after falling a revised 35,000 in September.

"The non-farm payrolls were about in line. But more importantly, there had been concern that September's would go from minus 40,000 to a revision of plus 100,000 and that didn't happen. There was no rise in average hourly earnings. There's no inflation out there," Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management said.
September payrolls were revised to minus 35,000. Average earnings per hour were unchanged at $11.91.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 36.15 points at 6,029.38 on Thursday after weak economic data suggested interest rates would remain low.
